result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.triad_type()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Classify the triad formed by three nodes of a directed graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.triad_type()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Classify the triad formed by three nodes of a directed graph. title: >- [Graph.triad_type()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Classify the triad formed by three nodes of a directed graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Classify the triad formed by three nodes of a directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L32873-L32927){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.triad_type(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Triad type](../assets/graphs/triad-type.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two copies of a directed graph on A, B, C, D: A points to B and C, B points to C, and C and D point at each other. Left copy: the triple A, B, C in the accent color is a transitive triad of three one-way arcs, type 030T. Right copy: B, C, D in teal has one mutual pair, one one-way pair and one empty pair, type 111D. The card gives both MAN codes." width="100%"} A triad is the subgraph induced by three nodes. Holland and Leinhardt's MAN scheme names each of the 16 possible triads by its number of Mutual, Asymmetric and Null dyads plus a letter for orientation (U up, D down, C cyclic, T transitive): `"003"` is empty, `"030T"` a transitive triple, `"030C"` a 3-cycle, `"300"` fully reciprocated. Triad types are the vocabulary of social network analysis for hierarchy, transitivity and reciprocity, and `triadic_census()` counts them over the whole graph. Parallel edges and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Three distinct nodes, as IDs or labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The triad's MAN code, one of `003, 012, 102, 021D, 021U, 021C, 111D, 111U, 030T, 030C, 201, 120D, 120U, 120C, 210, 300`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, or `nodes` is not three distinct existing nodes. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The code follows from the arcs among the three nodes, using NetworkX's `triad_type` rules on the induced subgraph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#bfada9dc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("A", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "C")]) g.triad_type(["A", "B", "C"]), g.triad_type(["B", "C", "D"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ('030T', '111D') ``` ::: :::
